Craster

No ratings yet
LAT 55.4796 LON -1.5934

Craster is one of Northumberland's most characterful coastal villages. With its working harbour, rugged coastline and views towards Dunstanburgh Castle, it is a great place to experience some of the county's most dramatic scenery.

Craster is best known for its small harbour, traditional fishing heritage and famous smoked kippers. The village is also the starting point for one of Northumberland's most popular coastal walks, following the shoreline towards the ruins of Dunstanburgh Castle. With sea views, rocky coastline and open countryside, Craster is an excellent place to explore on foot and enjoy a slower pace.

GETTING THERE

Craster is on the Northumberland coast, around 8 miles east of Alnwick. It is easiest to reach by car, with access from the A1 and local roads through Embleton and nearby villages. There is no railway station in Craster, so travelling by car is generally the most practical option.

AT A GLANCE

Good to know

PARKING

There is a public car park on the edge of Craster, close to the village and harbour. It can become busy during weekends and school holidays, particularly when the weather is good, so arriving earlier is advisable.

BEST TIME TO VISIT

Spring and summer are popular for coastal walks and longer days. Early mornings and later afternoons are often quieter, while autumn and winter can offer a dramatic atmosphere along the exposed coastline.
